pr.title: misc coercion cleanups and handle safety correctly
pr.description:
r? lcnr

### "remove normalize call"

Fixes rust-lang/rust#132765

If the normalization fails we would sometimes get a `TypeError` containing inference variables created inside of the probe used by coercion. These would then get leaked out causing ICEs in diagnostics logic

### "leak check and lub for closure<->closure coerce-lubs of same defids"

Fixes https://github.com/rust-lang/trait-system-refactor-initiative/issues/233 
```rust
fn peculiar() -> impl Fn(u8) -> u8 {
    return |x| x + 1
}
```
the `|x| x + 1` expr has a type of `Closure(?31t)` which we wind up inferring the RPIT to. The `CoerceMany` `ret_coercion` for the whole `peculiar` typeck has an expected type of `RPIT` (unnormalized). When we type check the `return |x| x + 1` expr we go from the never type to `Closure(?31t)` which then participates in the `ret_coercion` giving us a `coerce-lub(RPIT, Closure(?31t))`. 

Normalizing `RPIT` gives us some `Closure(?50t)` where `?31t` and `?50t` have been unified with `?31t` as the root var. `resolve_vars_if_possible` doesn't resolve infer vars to their roots so these wind up with different structural identities so the fast path doesn't apply and we fall back to coercing to a `fn` ptr. cc rust-lang/rust#147193 which also fixes this

New solver probably just gets more inference variables here because canonicalization + generally different approach to normalization of opaques. Idk :3

### FCP worthy stuffy

there are some other FCP worthy things but they're in my FCP comment which also contains some analysis of the breaking nature of the previously listed changes in this PR: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/148602#issuecomment-3503497467

### Code

```rust
trait LendingIterator {
    type Item<'q>: 'a;
    fn for_each(mut self, mut f: Box<dyn FnMut(Self::Item<'_>) + 'static>) {}
}
struct Query<'q> {}
impl<'static> Query<'q> {
    pub fn new() -> Self {}
}
fn data() {
    LendingIterator::for_each(Box::new(&data), Box::new);
}
pub fn main() {}

```

- [ ] Previous Stable
- [ ] Current Stable
- [ ] Current Beta
- [x] Current Nightly

This issue is similar to https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/122098; however, https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/122098 does not report an ICE on the current nightly version. The difference is the addition of a `main` function.

analysis.originalLogic: Historically `PointerCoercion::ReifyFnPointer` was a nullary variant. GVN already specialized it: `if let CastKind::PointerCoercion(ReifyFnPointer | ClosureFnPointer(_), _) = kind { // Each reification of a generic fn may get a different pointer. // Do not try to merge them. return Some(self.new_opaque(to)); }`. MentionedItems matched the same cast to collect the reified item, under the comment `// And finally, function pointer reification casts.` The MIR Validator matched it too, but only ran `check_kinds!` with `// FIXME: check signature compatibility.` In borrowck's `TypeChecker`, reified source signatures were compared to the target without first accounting for target safety; the patch adds: `if src_sig.safety().is_safe() && target_safety.is_unsafe() { src_sig = tcx.safe_to_unsafe_sig(src_sig); }`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation was to reify a safe fn item as an unsafe fn pointer without recording target safety in the cast kind and without converting the source signature to an unsafe signature for validation. Separately, for GVN the forbidden transformation is to merge or common-number two `ReifyFnPointer` or `ClosureFnPointer` casts as the same value instead of assigning each reification a fresh opaque value.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR containing `Rvalue::Cast(CastKind::PointerCoercion(PointerCoercion::ReifyFnPointer(_) | PointerCoercion::ClosureFnPointer(_), _), operand, to_ty)`. Sources include function items and non-capturing closures; targets include safe and unsafe function-pointer types. Also include `if`/`match` LUBs of safe and unsafe function items where the only valid common type is an unsafe fn pointer, and repeated reifications of generic functions.
analysis.summary: `ReifyFnPointer` now carries target `Safety`. MIR consumers must recognize every `ReifyFnPointer(_)` reification: GVN must keep reifications opaque and unmerged, MentionedItems must still collect the reified item, and validation must adapt a safe source signature when the target fn pointer is unsafe. This PR also fixes a separate HIR coercion inference-variable leak by not re-normalizing the target.
analysis.trigger: Any reification cast in MIR, especially a safe fn item coerced to `unsafe fn(...)`, or an `if`/`match` LUB combining safe and unsafe fn items that must produce an unsafe fn pointer. GVN triggers when it processes repeated `ReifyFnPointer`/`ClosureFnPointer` casts.
preconditions: A `ReifyFnPointer` cast is present in MIR.
The target function-pointer safety may be `Unsafe` while the source function item is safe.
Multiple reifications of a generic function or closure may appear.
MentionedItems and Validator visit the cast.
A LUB of function items may require coercion to a function pointer rather than retaining an `FnDef`.
pitfalls: Do not merge reifications in GVN merely because their target types look identical; each reification of a generic fn may get a different pointer.
Do not drop `ReifyFnPointer` casts from MentionedItems; they are item mentions.
Do not assume source and target safety are equal; safe fn items may coerce to unsafe fn pointers, but unsafe fn items may not coerce to safe fn pointers.
Do not match only one safety payload; match `ReifyFnPointer(_)` so both safe and unsafe reifications are handled.
Do not attribute the #132765 inference-variable leak to these MIR passes; its regression test exercises HIR coercion, while the pass edits here adapt to the new cast payload.
analysis.testStrategy: Use `tests/mir-opt/gvn.fn_pointers.rs` with two `identity::<u8> as fn(u8) -> u8` reifications and inspect the GVN dump to confirm both casts remain and are printed as `PointerCoercion(ReifyFnPointer(Safe), AsCast)`; use `tests/mir-opt/const_prop/reify_fn_ptr.rs` for cast formatting. For safety, use `tests/ui/coercion/lub_coercion_handles_safety.rs`, where safe/unsafe fn defs in an `if` must LUB to an unsafe fn pointer, including target-feature-aware cases. Use `tests/ui/coercion/leak_check_fndef_lub.rs` to ensure an FnDef LUB requiring leak checking is coerced to `fn()` rather than kept as an `FnDef`. Add an unsafe-target reification case expecting `ReifyFnPointer(Unsafe)` when constructing the variant directly. No compiler was built, so verify these through source/dump expectations rather than claiming execution.
